outline.rationale: The user is an experienced SWE exploring an AIPM transition, most worried about AI/ML technical depth. I skipped PM 101, software fundamentals, and resume/interview tactics per the confirmed understanding. Node 1 frames the role distinctively given they know both SWE and product. Node 2 directly addresses their core anxiety by calibrating what depth is essential vs. optional, preventing them from over-studying. Nodes 3-4 give the conceptual ML scaffolding an AIPM needs (mental models and failure modes), leveraging their ability to self-study coding. Nodes 5-6 cover the operational skills unique to AI products and ML team collaboration that differ from their SWE experience. Node 7 turns learning active via projects, which suits a SWE who can code. Node 8 grounds the exploration in concrete role/company realities since they're still deciding. Soft skills like roadmapping/stakeholder management are deliberately excluded as deprioritized. Nodes have low overlap and progress from role understanding to depth calibration to application.
